title: I worked at Amazon on an F-1 visa as layoffs mounted. Here's why I left for a semiconductor company.
summary:
My goal was to land a tech job and stay in the US after graduating.
About a month later, Amazon reached out with an online assessment for a software engineering role I'd applied for.
Amazon wasn't the only large tech company laying workers, so I wasn't sure I'd find the security I was looking for in Big Tech.
It was the type of role I'd been looking for — one that would let me work at the intersection of technology and business.
When I received the offer in April, I learned it also came with higher compensation than my Amazon job.

title: ⁠Is ICE using too much force? New poll shows big public opinion shift
summary:
ETMonths of immigration enforcement controversies have taken their toll, and new polling shows it could be a problem for Republicans heading into the midterms.
An earlier YouGov poll, which was conducted before the two shootings, found that most independents – 62% – believe ICE has gone too far.
Other polls from YouGov, AP-NORC and The Civic Health and Institutions Project found that only a fraction of independent voters support ICE's handling of immigration enforcement.
Some polls found that for most voters, immigration was their top issue.
Democrats, meanwhile, remain firmly opposed to the immigration enforcement operations underway, with 9 in 10 saying ICE has gone too far.

title: Ceuta mayor calls for migrant detention amid mass influx crisis
summary:
Thousands of migrants and asylum seekers in Ceuta face dire conditions, sparking political and social tensions in the Spanish territory.
Ceuta’s leader has demanded the detention and expulsion of thousands of asylum seekers and undocumented migrants roaming the streets in the Spanish North African territory after last month’s mass crossing from Morocco.
The Spanish government says 70,000 migrants and asylum seekers returned to Morocco within two days.
AdvertisementCeuta Mayor Vivas estimates that between 8,000 and 11,000 migrants are still in the Spanish territory and says the situation is “unsustainable”.
He disputes the government’s statistics that only 2,500 asylum seekers and undocumented migrants remain.
